open_points.subject: randomly minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random identifier generation, collision detection and retry for all five record types?
options: Each record-owning module mints its own and `store` rejects collisions
A separate lower-level identity/randomness module owns minting
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint and collision-check them atomically because it owns uniqueness and is the one writer.

open_points.subject: equal content submission semantics
open_points.text: `canonical_values` owns “A01 rules 1 and 4” but also “Must not own: Where a value is stored”; A01 rule 4 requires an existing record to be returned unchanged, nothing new recorded, and an equal contract not made current again.
open_points.question: Does `canonical_values` own only identity/equality calculation, or does it also own the persistence and current-selection behavior required when equal content already exists; if not, which record-owning module owns that behavior?
options: `canonical_values` only computes identity; `functions` and `flows` own the equal-submission behavior for their records
`store` owns an atomic get-or-return-existing policy used by every content record owner
`canonical_values` owns the entire A01 rule 4 behavior despite its persistence prohibition
open_points.default_guess: Limit `canonical_values` to identity calculation, with each aggregate-owning module enforcing A01 rule 4 through atomic store operations.
